FIRST-UP WORK: the DEC-303 (a1) ROUTE CHANGE (operator first-party via opum-doc, read by the leader on the record branch opum-ai/opum-doc#1932, commit e2ceee29; verify against opum-doc by ref with gh api, never its working copy). Verbatim from the record: 'THE ROUTE CHANGES. The operator first-party ... answering whether Python should come via pyright's language server or via glyph's own analyzer: native python support like typescript. glyph does NOT use a language server for Python. Items 1, 3 and 4 of DEC-303 are superseded. Item 2 (the same command contract per language, never a silent empty) and item 5 (the release floor; the tag waits for Python) stand.' Design (opum-doc, Article 5.1): (1) a native in-process indexer, no server process; tree-sitter's Python grammar (WASM build, no Python runtime); glyph owns the semantics: repository-local module and import resolution (absolute, relative, aliased, re-exported; src/, lib/, packages/*/src roots), scopes, class/method attribution, inheritance, constructor calls recorded against their class, decorators. (2) receiver types needing inference (obj.method() on an untyped value) are reported unresolved and COUNTED, never guessed; self, cls and known-class bindings ARE attributed; the parser sees every call so the unresolved count is exact (D1 settled). (3) adopted from the LSP packet: D2 A (one language per run), D4 A (additive contract fields recorded in ADR 0002), D5 B (exit 7 only when a first-party package root fails to resolve; count and name the rest). (4) GATE reusing the harness and the pinned requests ground truth: incoming recall >= 0.9 with Wilson lower bound >= 0.8 and precision >= 0.95, on requests AND on a held-out, less-annotated second repository whose ground truth is committed BEFORE any run; pyright's numbers are the baseline; a shortfall goes to opum-doc with the numbers. (5) ADR 0008 is REWRITTEN for the native design naming DEC-303 (a1) BEFORE any build slice; the LSP measurement stays committed as the baseline and the harness. DO NOT start build slices before the leader relays opum-doc's acceptance of the rewritten ADR; the leader named dispatch-floor for any slice (Sonnet writers, an Opus review per slice; a new runtime dependency such as a tree-sitter WASM package is a package.json change and needs the Opus review at the exact green head).

WHAT THE HARNESS AND THE PINNED requests SET GIVE THE SUCCESSOR (all in test/python-lsp-measurement/ on docs/GCLI-python-measurement; README there is the map): ground truth fixed before pyright ran (gt_rules.md, gt3_classified.json for psf/requests 3c7baaa05ab4aa49cc819ce3a819d260de19c157 src/requests: 46 seeded targets, 65 hand-classified true call sites, 9 zero-truth controls; fixtures/expected.json for 18 fixture targets; gt_rules_addendum.md lists everything learned or decided afterwards: the alias set gt4_alias.json (post hoc, a census), the post-hoc constructor mapping, no pre-registered bar). Tooling takes all paths as arguments: gt1_enumerate.py (ast enumeration, seed 303 regenerates targets byte-identically), alias_enum.py, harness.mjs (LSP client; exits non-zero on no answers/errors), score.py, union.py (per site AND per target, recall and precision, Wilson plus a cluster bootstrap over the 37 targets with a true site), strata.py, compare_runs.py, import_probe.py; derived/ holds the deterministic inputs; results/ every scored output with gzipped raw in results/raw/; results/ground-truth.bundle and ground-truth-provenance.txt (provenance is self-asserted, not independent timestamps). Re-score without any server: python3 and gunzip only (README). For a NATIVE indexer the scorer needs only a new raw producer: union.py/score.py read the harness JSON shape (targets[key].incoming list of {file,line,col}); emit that shape from the native index to reuse them. BASELINE NUMBERS to beat or match (pyright 1.1.414, requests, 65 sites): incoming 58/65 default platform and 59/65 with pythonPlatform All; union with outgoing plus constructor mapping 65/65 (an IN-SAMPLE FIT, the mapping was designed on the six sites it recovers); alias calls (15 sites) incoming 2/15, outgoing 15/15. The cluster-robust lower bound for incoming alone on All is 0.788, below the 0.8 gate; the held-out second repository's ground truth must be committed (and the scorer rules fixed) before any native run. KNOWN FAILURES worth designing against natively: constructor calls attribute to the class not __init__; aliased imports (incoming misses them); decorator applications; unreachable/platform-conditional code; absolute first-party imports silently lost when the source root is unlisted (the harness showed 0/5 with an out-of-repo root unless extraPaths was set; definition at imports returned none exactly then).

PROCESS RULES LEARNED (capture the rule, not the incident): (1) REVIEWER ROUNDS: the leader spawns a fresh read-only reviewer per head (Opus for contract/release/dependency/architecture work and README claims; a Sonnet reviewer for test-only PRs); I create a detached worktree (git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/review-<name>-<sha7> <sha>, leave it registered) and send the leader its PATH and the head; a new head means a new (delta) review, and a verdict is for the head it names, so say which items a newer head already answers. The ADR for GCLI-66 took five rounds; each round's defects were real (the bar quantity, fit labelling, a silent-failure path, unscored shipped channel): answer every numbered item RESOLVED/OPEN/DISPUTED with a file and phrase, do not narrow limits to look better. (2) NUMBERS: quote no number you cannot tie to a committed file; compute intervals with a committed script, label any estimate as an estimate, label post-hoc elements post hoc, withdraw wrong figures explicitly (I once reported a name-matched union that lost alias calls). (3) Ownership guard refuses shell-built write targets ($VAR/path), so use literal scratchpad paths and the Write tool; a composed command with git commit text on a branch named main/dev trips the trunk guard (checkout in a separate call); git log needs --no-ext-diff --no-textconv; the guard blocks git bundle/init on unresolved targets (use literal paths). (4) Quest: --acceptance-criteria replacement cannot be combined with --check-ac in one edit; quest task create prints YAML (do not grep it to a pipe and re-run: a failed grep once created a duplicate, GCLI-62); a dependency edge needs the target record on the branch; a task must be started before it can be completed (To Do to Done is refused); never edit .quest JSON by hand. (5) lore sync adds log entries from git history (additive); revert docs/log.md if a sync loses or duplicates a dated entry. (6) Scratch, not the repo: install and clone untrusted material (pyright, requests) in the session scratchpad, python3 -I over untrusted files, no package.json or lockfile change from measurement. (7) Leader rules: stagger pushes, one re-run per red PR, no timeouts raised to mask load, Check can still flake (headroom about 2x), the leader lands, a hold is a label (GCLI-60 and GCLI-64 carry it).
